Fig. 2
Traction-assisted endoscopic submucosal dissection for a pyloric neoplasm. (A) A slightly elevated lesion was observed in the 12−3 o’clock quadrant of the pylorus. (B) Retroflexion was impossible because of the narrow duodenal bulb. Therefore, mucosal marking and incision were performed around the tumor, excluding the distal portion, after indigo carmine chromoendoscopy. (C) Submucosal dissection of the proximal portion was performed. (D) After traction using an endoclip with dental floss, submucosal dissection and mucosal cutting of the distal portion were performed. (E) The lesion was completely removed. (F) Resected specimen.

summary.text: The Figure 2 caption describes a slightly elevated pyloric neoplasm in the 12−3 o’clock quadrant. A narrow duodenal bulb prevented retroflexion. Indigo carmine chromoendoscopy, marking/incision, proximal dissection, dental-floss endoclip traction and distal dissection/cutting led to complete lesion removal.
